en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having one of the most perfectly symmetrical cone shapes in the world.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, locally called the monkey-eating eagle, has a distinctive shaggy crest of brown feathers.
The Cagayan River is the longest and largest river in the Philippines, flowing through the Cagayan Valley.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake in the island of Mindanao and the second largest lake in the entire Philippines.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The island province of Batanes is the northernmost province of the Philippines and is known for its traditional stone houses.
The Philippine tarsier, found in the forests of Bohol, is one of the smallest primates in the world and has enormous eyes.
The Sibuyan Sea separates the islands of Luzon, Mindoro, Panay, and Masbate, and is home to the Romblon island group.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel, an essential mineral primarily mined in the provinces of Surigao and Zambales.
Baguio City, located in the Cordillera Administrative Region, has a cooler climate than most Philippine cities because of its high elevation.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting over six hundred marine species.
